concepts.title: รัน JavaScript ครั้งแรก: Console, node file.js, ตัวแปร let/const ชนิดข้อมูล และ === กับ ==
concepts.covers: Three ways to run JS: browser DevTools Console (F12), node REPL (> prompt, .exit), and node file.js; console.log. let vs const (and why not var), naming in camelCase, the 7 primitive types + object, typeof (including typeof null === 'object' quirk), number pitfalls (0.1 + 0.2, Number('12a') -> NaN, Number.isNaN, parseInt('42px')), arithmetic and % and **, string basics and template literals `${}` with toFixed(2) and toLocaleString('th-TH'), === vs == (0 == '' true, null == undefined true, '5' === 5 false), truthy/falsy list. Example file ~/projects/js-lab/c01-basics/basics.js: a coffee order (const item = 'ชาไทยเย็น', price 45, qty 3, let discount = 0.1, isMember = true, coupon = null, note undefined) prints each value with typeof, computes subtotal 135 and total 121.5 printed as `ยอดสุทธิ 121.50 บาท`, shows 0.1 + 0.2, (0.1 + 0.2).toFixed(2), a comparison table of == vs === for 6 pairs, and Boolean() of falsy values. Run: node basics.js. Also show the same 3 lines typed in the Browser Console (data-env app, label 'JavaScript · Browser Console'). Mistakes: TypeError: Assignment to constant variable., ReferenceError: totl is not defined, SyntaxError: Identifier 'price' has already been declared, NaN from adding undefined.

concepts.title: เงื่อนไข ลูป และฟังก์ชัน: if/switch, for/for...of/while, Arrow Function, Default และ Rest Parameters
concepts.covers: if/else if/else, ternary, switch with break, logical && || !, for (let i...), for...of over arrays/strings, while, break/continue; function declaration vs function expression vs arrow function (implicit return, returning an object needs parentheses), default parameters, rest parameters (...nums), return vs console.log, pure functions. Example file ~/projects/js-lab/c02-functions/grades.js: const scores = [95, 82, 74, 61, 48, 105]; function toGrade(score) with if chain A>=80 B>=70 C>=60 D>=50 else F, throws nothing yet (invalid >100 or <0 skipped with continue in the loop); for...of with an index counter prints `คนที่ 1: 95 -> A` ...; counts passes (>=50); arrow function average = (...nums) => ... ; function greet(name = 'ผู้เรียน', greeting = 'สวัสดี'); switch on day 'sat'/'sun' -> 'วันหยุด'. Run: node grades.js. Mistakes: forgetting return (function returns undefined), arrow `() => { total: 1 }` returning undefined, infinite while loop (forgot i++), TypeError: toGrade is not a function when a const arrow is called before definition (ReferenceError: Cannot access 'toGrade' before initialization).

concepts.title: HTML และ CSS ที่ต้องรู้ก่อนแตะ DOM: Semantic Tags, Form, Selector, Box Model และ Flexbox
concepts.covers: Taught from zero because no other topic covers it. Document skeleton (<!DOCTYPE html>, html lang='th', meta charset/viewport, title), semantic tags (header, nav, main, section, article, footer), headings order, img alt, a form with label for/id, input types (text, email, number), required/min/max attributes, button type='submit'. CSS: linking style.css, selectors (type, .class, #id, descendant, :hover, :focus-visible), specificity basics, the box model (content/padding/border/margin, box-sizing: border-box), display block/inline, Flexbox (display:flex, gap, justify-content, align-items, flex-wrap, flex: 1), one media query (max-width: 600px) and CSS custom properties (--brand). Example folder ~/projects/js-lab/c03-html-css with index.html (a profile card page for somchai: header, nav with 3 links, main with 3 article cards in a flex row, and a contact form) and style.css. Open with python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1 and http://127.0.0.1:8000. Verifiable output: a check script check-layout.mjs run with Node + Playwright in the writer's sandbox only (learners see the same values in DevTools > Elements > Computed) printing the computed width of a .card with box-sizing content-box vs border-box (e.g. width 200px + padding 16px + border 2px -> 236 vs 200), the flex direction and the card positions at 1024px vs 375px viewport. Present the learner-facing verification as DevTools Computed panel values and paste real numbers. Mistakes: CSS not applied because of wrong href path (404 in Network tab), label not linked (for/id mismatch), unclosed tag breaking layout, flex set on the child instead of the parent.

concepts.title: Array และ Array Methods: map, filter, reduce, find, some/every และกับดักของ sort
concepts.covers: Creating arrays, index, length, push/pop/shift/unshift, includes, indexOf, slice vs splice (mutating vs not), for...of vs forEach, then the core higher-order methods map, filter, reduce (with an initial value), find/findIndex, some/every, join, chaining; sort pitfalls: default sort converts to strings ([10, 9, 1, 100].sort() -> [1, 10, 100, 9]), sort mutates (use toSorted() available in Node 20+ or [...arr].sort()), compare function (a, b) => a - b, localeCompare('th') for Thai names. Example file ~/projects/js-lab/c04-arrays/cart.js with the shared cart sample data (see notes): total with reduce = 405, names with price >= 40 via filter+map, find the first item with qty >= 3, some(qty === 0), every(price > 0), sorted by price descending without mutating (prove original order unchanged), numbers [10, 9, 1, 100] default sort vs numeric sort, and Thai names sorted with localeCompare. Run: node cart.js. Mistakes: reduce on an empty array without initial value -> TypeError: Reduce of empty array with no initial value, forgetting return inside a map with braces (array of undefined), using forEach and expecting a return value, sort without compare function.

concepts.title: Object, Destructuring, Spread, Optional Chaining (?.) และ Nullish Coalescing (??)
concepts.covers: Object literals, dot vs bracket access, adding/deleting keys, shorthand properties, methods, Object.keys/values/entries/fromEntries, for...of over Object.entries; references vs copies (const obj can still change; shallow copy with spread {...obj}, structuredClone for deep copy); array and object destructuring with defaults and renaming, destructuring in function parameters; spread/rest for arrays and objects (merging settings, later keys win); optional chaining user?.address?.province and arr?.[0] and fn?.(); ?? vs || (0 and '' are kept by ??); JSON.stringify(obj, null, 2) and JSON.parse preview. Example file ~/projects/js-lab/c05-objects/profile.js with user somchai: {username: 'somchai', name: 'สมชาย ใจดี', age: 28, address: {province: 'ขอนแก่น'}, skills: ['HTML', 'CSS', 'JavaScript'], settings: {theme: 'dark', fontSize: 0}}; prints destructured values, a merged settings object from defaults {theme: 'light', fontSize: 16, lang: 'th'} via spread, fontSize via || (16, wrong) vs ?? (0, right), user.company?.name -> undefined, shows that a spread copy shares the nested address (mutation leaks) and structuredClone does not, and Object.entries loop. Run: node profile.js. Mistakes: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'province'), TypeError: Cannot destructure property 'name' of 'undefined' as it is undefined., shallow copy surprise, using || where 0 is valid.

concepts.title: ES Modules และ npm: import/export, package.json, npm scripts และการติดตั้งแพ็กเกจ
concepts.covers: Why modules; named vs default export, import { a as b }, import * as ns; Node rules: "type": "module" in package.json (npm init -y on npm 11 sets "type": "commonjs", so run npm pkg set type=module), relative paths need ./ and .js extension, top-level await; browser <script type="module" src="main.js"> needs http:// (file:// blocked by CORS), modules are deferred and strict; reading CommonJS (require/module.exports) without writing it; package.json fields, scripts (start, test), npm install dayjs@1.11.23 (dependencies, ^ semver, package-lock.json committed, node_modules ignored), npm install --save-dev, npm ci, npx caution, npm audit, typosquatting. Example project ~/projects/js-lab/c06-modules: src/price.js (export const VAT_RATE = 0.07; export function withVat(amount); export default function formatBaht(n) -> '1,070.00 บาท' using toLocaleString('th-TH', {minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2})), src/due.js using dayjs to add 7 days to a fixed date dayjs('2026-10-19') -> '2026-10-26' (fixed date so output is deterministic), index.js importing both, and "scripts": {"start": "node index.js"}; run npm start. Show the real npm install output pattern ("added 1 package, and audited 2 packages in 1s" timing varies). Mistakes: SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module, Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find module '/home/somchai/projects/js-lab/c06-modules/src/price' (missing .js), SyntaxError: The requested module './src/price.js' does not provide an export named 'formatBaht' (default vs named), browser CORS error from file://.

concepts.title: DOM: เลือก แก้ไข และสร้าง Element (querySelector, textContent, classList, createElement)
concepts.covers:
What the DOM tree is (HTML -> objects), document.querySelector/querySelectorAll (NodeList, forEach, Array.from), getElementById; reading/changing textContent vs innerHTML (and why innerHTML with user data is an XSS risk), attributes (setAttribute, dataset via data-*), classList add/remove/toggle/contains, style vs classes; creating nodes with createElement, append, prepend, remove, replaceChildren, DocumentFragment; render-from-data pattern (state array -> render() rebuilds a list). Example folder ~/projects/js-lab/c07-dom: index.html (a todo-style 'รายการที่ต้องเรียน' page with
    and

    ), style.css (.done line-through), app.js (type=module) with const topics = [{id:1,title:'HTML',done:true},{id:2,title:'CSS',done:true},{id:3,title:'DOM',done:false},{id:4,title:'Fetch',done:false}] rendering

  • items with createElement + textContent + dataset.id and classList.toggle('done'), summary 'เรียนแล้ว 2 จาก 4 หัวข้อ', plus console.log of querySelectorAll('li').length and the first li's outerHTML. Learner runs via http.server and sees the console in DevTools; writer verifies with Playwright and pastes the real browser console output into a block labelled 'JavaScript · Browser Console' (data-env app) or an out block, and shows the rendered list text. Also show an innerHTML XSS demo with the string '' rendered safely via textContent. concepts.title: Events, Event Delegation และ Forms: addEventListener, preventDefault, FormData และ Validation
concepts.covers: addEventListener('click'|'input'|'submit'|'keydown'), the event object (target, currentTarget, key), removing listeners, bubbling and event delegation with closest() on a parent so new elements work automatically, preventDefault on form submit, reading values with FormData and Object.fromEntries, built-in constraint validation (required, type=email, minlength, pattern, checkValidity, setCustomValidity, :invalid/:user-invalid styling), custom validation messages in Thai shown in an element with aria-live, accessibility (label, aria-invalid, aria-describedby), keyboard events and not using div as a button. Example folder ~/projects/js-lab/c08-events: index.html with a register form (username, email, age number min 15, password minlength 8) and a <ul id="choices"> of 4 <button data-index> answer buttons; app.js validates and on success logs JSON.stringify of the form data (password masked) and shows 'สมัครสำเร็จ: somchai'; delegation on #choices logs `เลือกตัวเลือกที่ 2: let` and adds .selected; keydown 1-4 shortcut selects. Writer verifies with a Playwright script that fills the form (invalid then valid) and clicks/presses keys, pasting the real console output. Mistakes: page reloads on submit (forgot preventDefault / listening on button click instead of form submit), event.target is the inner <span> not the button (use closest('button')), listener attached before elements exist / to each item losing it after re-render, addEventListener('click', handle()) calling the function immediately.

concepts.title: Scope, Closures, Hoisting, this และ Classes
concepts.covers: Global/function/block scope, lexical scope, closures (counter factory, private state, once()), the classic var-in-loop with setTimeout bug vs let; hoisting: function declarations hoisted, var hoisted as undefined, let/const in the TDZ (ReferenceError: Cannot access 'x' before initialization); 'this': method call vs plain call (undefined in strict mode/modules), losing this when passing a method as a callback, fixing with arrow functions or bind, arrow functions have no own this; classes: constructor, methods, getters, static methods, private fields #balance, extends/super, instanceof; classes are syntax over prototypes (brief). Example file ~/projects/js-lab/c09-closures/closures-classes.js (a .js file; ~/projects/js-lab/package.json has "type": "module"): makeCounter() closure, var vs let loop printing 3 3 3 vs 0 1 2 with setTimeout 0, hoisting demo with try/catch catching the TDZ ReferenceError, class BankAccount { #balance; constructor(owner, balance = 0); deposit(); withdraw() throws RangeError('ยอดเงินไม่พอ'); get balance(); static fromJSON() } and class SavingsAccount extends BankAccount with addInterest(rate); owner 'somchai', deposit 500, withdraw 200, interest 0.02; shows the lost-this TypeError when passing account.deposit as a callback and the bind fix. Run: node closures-classes.js. Mistakes: lost this when a method is passed as a callback (run it and paste the real TypeError, which for a private field is 'TypeError: Cannot read private member #balance from an object whose class did not declare it'), ReferenceError from the TDZ, SyntaxError: Private field '#balance' must be declared in an enclosing class, forgetting super() -> ReferenceError: Must call super constructor in derived class before accessing 'this' or returning from derived constructor.

concepts.title: Error Handling, JSON และ localStorage: try/catch/finally, Error Types, Custom Error และการบันทึกข้อมูลในเบราว์เซอร์
concepts.covers: throw, try/catch/finally, built-in error types (TypeError, RangeError, SyntaxError from JSON.parse, ReferenceError), error.name/message/stack, rethrowing unknown errors, custom class ValidationError extends Error with this.name, error.cause (new Error('...', { cause })), fail fast vs graceful fallback, never swallowing errors silently; JSON.stringify/parse with nested data, Date and undefined pitfalls; localStorage setItem/getItem/removeItem (strings only), key namespacing like 'js-lab:settings', safe load with try/catch and default value, storage quota and private mode exceptions, not storing secrets/tokens. Part A node file ~/projects/js-lab/c10-errors/errors.js: parseAge(input) throwing ValidationError for '', 'abc', -5, 200 and returning 28 for '28'; safeParse(jsonText, fallback) handling broken JSON '{"theme": "dark",}' (real SyntaxError message from Node); a loop printing name/message for each case. Part B browser folder ~/projects/js-lab/c10-errors/web: index.html + storage-demo.js with createStore(storage, key) save/load functions (storage passed in so it is testable) that saves {theme:'dark', fontSize:18, lastVisit:'2026-10-19'}, reloads it, then simulates corrupt data 'not-json' and falls back to defaults; writer verifies in Playwright (reload page to prove persistence) and pastes real console output; learner checks DevTools > Application > Local Storage. Mistakes: SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'o', "not-json" is not valid JSON (message differs by engine: show the real V8 text), storing an object directly gives '[object Object]', catch block that hides the error, ReferenceError: localStorage is not defined when running browser code in Node.

concepts.title: Asynchronous JavaScript: Callback, Promise, async/await, fetch และ Event Loop
concepts.covers: Why async (single thread, non-blocking I/O); callbacks and callback hell; Promise states (pending/fulfilled/rejected), new Promise, then/catch/finally, Promise.all vs allSettled vs race vs any; async/await with try/catch, sequential vs parallel awaits (timing difference 600ms vs 300ms shown with Date.now, rounded so output is stable, e.g. 'ใช้เวลาประมาณ 0.6 วินาที'); the event loop: call stack, Web APIs, microtask queue (promises, queueMicrotask) vs macrotask queue (setTimeout), demo with numbered logs whose order is deterministic: 1 sync, 2 sync, promise microtasks, then setTimeout; fetch: response.ok and status check (fetch does not reject on 404), response.json(), AbortController / AbortSignal.timeout(3000), loading data/questions.json from a local server. Example folder ~/projects/js-lab/c11-async: event-loop.js (node), parallel.js (node, delay helper with setTimeout wrapped in a Promise), and fetch-demo.js run with Node 24 built-in fetch against python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1 serving data/questions.json (the same 3 questions as Part 1) plus a missing.json 404, using Promise.allSettled and printing fulfilled/rejected. Mistakes: forgetting await (prints Promise { <pending> }), await in a non-async function inside a regular script/CommonJS -> SyntaxError: await is only valid in async functions and the top level bodies of modules, unhandled rejection crashing Node (show the real error format), TypeError: fetch failed when the server is not running (cause ECONNREFUSED), forEach with async callbacks not waiting.

concepts.title: Debugging และ Testing: DevTools, node --inspect และ Unit Test ด้วย node:test
concepts.covers: Reading stack traces (file:line:column), console.table/group/time/assert, debugger; statement, DevTools Sources breakpoints (line, conditional, logpoint), Step over/into/out, Scope/Watch/Call Stack panels, Pause on exceptions, Network and Application tabs; Node: node --inspect-brk app.js + chrome://inspect, VS Code JavaScript Debug Terminal, node --watch; testing with node:test: test/describe/it, node:assert/strict (equal, deepEqual, throws, rejects), node --test auto-discovery (*.test.js, test/ folder), npm test, hooks beforeEach, mock.fn() to count calls, mock.timers to test a countdown without waiting, testing async functions; designing testable code (pure functions, pass dependencies like random/storage in). Example project ~/projects/js-lab/c12-testing ("type": "module", "scripts": {"test": "node --test"}): src/countdown.js exporting startCountdown(seconds, onTick, onDone) using setInterval/clearInterval, src/stats.js exporting average(nums) (throws TypeError on empty array) and a buggy-on-purpose median(nums) that mutates the input via sort without compare (the debugging story: find it with a breakpoint/test, then fix with toSorted((a,b)=>a-b)); test/stats.test.js and test/countdown.test.js using mock.timers.enable({ apis: ['setInterval'] }) and mock.timers.tick(1000). Show the real node --test output first failing (with the assertion diff) then passing (TAP-like spec reporter summary lines ℹ tests 7 ℹ pass 7 ℹ fail 0; duration_ms varies). Mistakes: test file not discovered (wrong name like stats.spec.js outside test/), assert.equal on objects -> AssertionError (use deepEqual), testing an async function without await/return (test passes falsely), Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND] from a wrong ../src path.

mini_project.name: Interactive Quiz App
mini_project.summary: A portfolio-quality vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript quiz app at ~/projects/quiz-app with no build step and no runtime dependencies: questions are loaded with fetch from data/questions.json, the UI is rendered from state with the DOM, answers come from click (event delegation) and keys 1-4, each question has a 15-second timer, the score and percent are shown at the end, the high score persists in localStorage under key quiz-app:highscore, the UI is accessible (buttons, focus management, aria-live, not color-only, prefers-reduced-motion, responsive with Flexbox), it is served locally with python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1, the pure logic is unit-tested with node:test (at least 8 tests in test/quiz.test.js and test/storage.test.js), and it is published to GitHub Pages as https://somchai.github.io/quiz-app/.
features: Folder structure exactly as in Part 1 Step 14: index.html, style.css, data/questions.json, src/quiz.js, src/storage.js, src/main.js, test/quiz.test.js, test/storage.test.js, package.json, .gitignore, README.md (keep the tree as listed; no .nojekyll needed)
data/questions.json: an array of exactly 10 question objects {id, question, choices[4], answer (0-based index)}; ids 1-3 are identical to Part 1 Step 12; ids 4-10 are fixed in notes

src/quiz.js (pure, no DOM): createQuiz(questions, { shuffle = false, random = Math.random } = {}) returns state {questions, index: 0, score: 0, answers: [], finished: false}; validateQuestions(data) throws TypeError with a Thai message for non-array/empty/malformed items; currentQuestion(state); answer(state, choiceIndex) returns a NEW state (immutable) with {correct: boolean}; timeout(state) records a null answer as wrong; next(state); percent(score, total) (same rules as Part 1 score.js: Math.round, RangeError when total is not a positive integer); shuffle(array, random) Fisher-Yates returning a new array; remainingSeconds(startedAtMs, nowMs, limit = 15) clamped to 0

src/storage.js: loadHighScore(storage = globalThis.localStorage) returns 0 when missing/corrupt/negative; saveHighScore(score, storage) only writes when higher and returns the new high score; key constant HIGH_SCORE_KEY = 'quiz-app:highscore'; stores JSON {score, percent, date} and never throws when storage is unavailable

src/main.js: loads 'data/questions.json' with a RELATIVE path via fetch, checks response.ok, shows a loading state, an error state with a 'ลองใหม่' button, renders 3 screens (start, question, result) by toggling the hidden attribute; event delegation on #choices; keydown 1-4; 15-second countdown per question with setInterval/clearInterval shown in a <progress> and text; correct/wrong feedback in an aria-live='polite' region with both color and text (✓ ถูกต้อง / ✗ ผิด คำตอบที่ถูกคือ ...); 'ข้อต่อไป' button; focus moves to the question heading (tabindex=-1) on each new question; result screen shows score, percent, high score and a 'เล่นอีกครั้ง' button
style.css: CSS custom properties, mobile-first, Flexbox for choices, .is-correct/.is-wrong classes, :focus-visible outline, @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)

Tests: npm test runs node --test; at least 8 tests total covering createQuiz, answer immutability, timeout, percent edge cases, shuffle with a seeded fake random, validateQuestions errors, remainingSeconds clamp, loadHighScore/saveHighScore with an in-memory fake storage (a Map-backed object with getItem/setItem) including corrupt JSON; real output pasted

Browser verification: the writer runs a Playwright script (sandbox only, not part of the project tree) that serves the folder, plays all 10 questions answering with keys and clicks, checks the result text and that the high score survives a reload; Part 4 shows the learner-facing manual checklist plus the real observed text

README.md template with features, screenshot placeholder, how to run (python3 -m http.server), how to test (npm test), tech used, what I learned; push to GitHub repo somchai/quiz-app and enable GitHub Pages (Deploy from a branch, main, / (root))
mini_project.stack: Vanilla HTML5, CSS3 and JavaScript (ES2023, ES Modules, no framework, no bundler, no runtime npm dependencies); Node.js 24.22.0 LTS via nvm v0.40.8 (must also run on 26.12.0) for node:test and node:assert/strict; npm 11 bundled with Node 24; Python 3.12.3 http.server for local serving; Chrome/Edge latest with DevTools and Lighthouse; Git 2.43.0 + GitHub Pages; optional dev tools ESLint 10.13.0 and Prettier 3.9.10

Module convention: all JavaScript is ES Modules (import/export, never require) and uses .js files thanks to "type": "module". Use relative paths without a leading slash (fetch('data/questions.json')).

Code style: 2-space indent, single quotes, semicolons, const by default and let only when reassigned, never var except in the c09 hoisting demo, === always, camelCase names, Thai text in UI strings and comments, English identifiers. Format money with n.toLocaleString('th-TH', { minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 }) + ' บาท' (e.g. 1,070.00 บาท).
